market_view: The HMM classifies the current regime as calm_bull. Momentum across the board is strongly positive — all 17 names screened show positive 252-day returns. Macro data was unavailable due to a system error, but the calm_bull regime and broad positive momentum suggest a constructive environment. The alternatives agent flagging 'stressed' is a yellow flag worth monitoring for regime transition risk.
regime_assessment: Calm bull regime confirmed by HMM. Three of four quant agents agree on a risk-on posture. The alternatives agent's stressed signal suggests we should maintain some defensive allocation (BIL, KMLM) as insurance. No past verdicts available for this regime to benchmark against.

quant_overrides.reason: SNDK shows +3372% 252-day momentum which is almost certainly a data artifact from the WDC/SNDK merger/corporate action. Excluding to avoid stale/distorted price data. WDC retained at reduced weight instead.

Macro agent recommended 8.2% UUP but in a calm_bull regime with strong equity momentum, dollar-long positioning is contrarian. Replaced with additional international and commodity exposure which better fits the regime.

Alternatives agent recommended DBA at 36% but its 252-day momentum is only +5.2%, the weakest of all candidates. Consolidated commodity exposure into PDBC and DBB which have stronger momentum profiles.
Retained base metals exposure (DBB, +39% momentum) as a macro diversifier but at reduced weight relative to the macro agent's recommendation, reallocating to equity names with stronger momentum.

key_risks: Regime transition risk: alternatives agent sees 'stressed' while HMM says calm_bull — possible early warning of regime change
Momentum crowding: many positions have extreme 252-day momentum; a momentum reversal would hit the portfolio hard
EM/Asia concentration: ~21% in EM equity (EWY+EWT+EEM) creates geopolitical concentration risk (Korea, Taiwan, China)
Data center/AI theme concentration: VRT, VICR, SATS, WDC all correlate to the same secular theme
Commodity direction: ~13% in commodities (PDBC+DBB) could drag in a deflationary scenario
Macro data unavailability: unable to verify yield curve, credit spreads, or CPI — flying partially blind on macro conditions
Annualized vol of ~20% is elevated; daily VaR-95 of -1.93% means ~3% drawdown days are possible
what_could_be_wrong: The biggest risk is that the calm_bull regime is late-cycle and about to transition. The alternatives agent's 'stressed' reading could be the canary in the coal mine. Extreme momentum in many names (SATS +499%, VICR +535%, WDC +873%) may reflect crowded trades or data artifacts rather than sustainable trends. Without macro data (yield curve, credit spreads, unemployment), I cannot confirm whether fundamentals support the regime classification. If we are at peak momentum in a late-cycle bull, this portfolio would suffer significant drawdowns. The 7% BIL and 6% KMLM provide some cushion but may be insufficient in a sharp correction.
